previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with primary progressive multiple sclerosis, neurogenic bladder with a suprapubic catheter, and a history of recurrent multidrug-resistant urinary tract infections, was admitted due to persistent fevers and malaise despite outpatient treatment with Bactrim for a suspected UTI. He presented with dizziness and weakness but no urinary symptoms. Initial evaluation showed no leukocytosis, and imaging revealed no abscess or obstructive uropathy. Urine culture grew Proteus mirabilis, resistant to Bactrim but susceptible to piperacillin-tazobactam. He was treated with IV antibiotics, transitioned to IV ceftriaxone, and discharged on oral cefpodoxime for a 10-day course. During admission, he was evaluated for dysphagia, with speech and swallow recommending a ground diet and supervised feeding. His stage II-III sacral and ischial pressure ulcers were managed with debridement and wound care, and plans were made for home support including a new mattress and cushion. Anemia and skin flaking were managed supportively. He was discharged home with services, stable and improving.

Brief Hospital Course:
***anticipated length of stay in rehab less than 30 days***

___ with a h/o advanced MS, neurogenic bladder w/ indwelling 
catheter and recurrent UTIs including MDR organisms, spastic 
extremities with ___ immobility and associated sacral ulcers, who 
presented from home due to increased lethargy and fever.  He was 
found to have septic shock from urinary source, also with distal 
femoral fracture managed non-operatively.  His UTI was 
ultimately found to be due to a multi-drug resistant 
Pseudomonas, ultimately treated with Zosyn per infectious 
Disease.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
===============================
# Septic Shock due to UTI
Pt with a history of multiple UTIs (Pseudomonas, E.coli, 
Enterococcus, Klebsiella) with an admission UA showing WBC >182, 
positive nitrites. Also with a history of neurogenic bladder 
with indwelling suprapubic cath.  Initially required ICU 
admission, but quickly stabilized with low dose Levophed and IV 
fluids.  Other than urine, no other source of infection 
identified (see below - but his knee swelling was ultimately due 
to a fracture, and the arthrocentesis was a dry tap).  Urology 
exchanged the SPT catheter on ___.  He was initially on 
Vancomycin and Meropenem, later narrowed to Zosyn monotherapy.  
On ___, despite quick clinical improvement on Zosyn, speciation 
and sensitivities revealed a very resistant pseudomonas 
aeruginosa in the urine, and ID was consulted.  Despite 
""intermediate"" sensitivity to Zosyn, per ID recommendations, we 
did an extended Zosyn infusion time (over 3 hours).  He 
continued to remain hemodynamically stable.  PICC line was 
placed so he can complete a full 2 week course of Zosyn.  The 
last day of Zosyn is ___.

# Left distal femur fracture
Presented with knee swelling.  Xray showed impacted distal 
femoral metadiaphysis fracture with dorsal displacement and 
ventral angulation of the fracture apex. Ortho was consulted.  
It was felt to be likely subacute.  Ortho recommended hinged 
left knee brace, and follow up in clinic in 2 weeks.  
Arthrocentesis revealed a dry tap, so infection very unlikely.  
Continue brace and no weight bearing until ___ clinic 
appointment.

# Constipation:  Presented with significant constipation and 
stool burden on KUB.  Colorectal surgery was consulted, 
recommending daily tap water irrigation and aggressive PO bowel 
regimen.

# Multiple Sclerosis
Pt with suprapubic cath, which was changed on ___ by 
Urology. Continued oxybutynin.  He has a Baclofen pump which was 
due for a refill while admitted.  This was refilled by the 
Chronic Pain Service on ___ while he was here.

# H/o tobacco use - provided with nicotine patch

# Anemia:  Hgb 11.3 on admission, then down to mid-8's after 
IVF, likely due to dilutional effect.  It was subsequently 
uptrending.  Retic index low, likely hypoproliferative.  No 
gross evidence of bleeding.  Started iron supplement

# Sacral Decubitus Ulcer:  Wounds appear clear, well healing, no 
e/o infection.  Continued Vitamin C to promote healing.  Stopped 
Zinc, as this is usually done for a defined course only.

# H/o recurrent UTI's:  Has seen ID as outpatient, recently 
started on Macrobid.  Macrobid was stopped due to 
ineffectiveness.  He will follow up with ID as an outpatient.

# HLD - continue home Ezetimibe

# CAD prevention - continue home ASA

# Psych - continue home Citalopram, Mirtazipine

# GERD - continue home Omeprazole 

# Nutrition - continue Multivitamin, Vitamin D

EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PORTABLE AP)

INDICATION:  History: ___ with MS, febrile, AMS// ?cpd

TECHNIQUE:  Chest PA and lateral

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph ___ and CT chest ___

FINDINGS: 

Heart size is normal.  Mediastinal and hilar contours are unremarkable. 
Pulmonary vasculature is not engorged.  Patchy retrocardiac opacity is again
demonstrated without focal consolidation.  No pleural effusion or pneumothorax
is present.  Cervical spinal fusion hardware is incompletely assessed.

IMPRESSION: 

Patchy retrocardiac opacity, as seen previously, likely atelectasis.  No new
focal consolidation.

INDICATION:  History: ___ with MS and new onset lethargy with probable UTI,
also with erythematous and swollen knee without pain// evaluate for signs of
infection and injury

TECHNIQUE:  Left knee, three views

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

An impacted fracture of the distal femoral metaphysis with dorsal displacement
of the dominant distal fracture fragment and angulation of the fracture
fracture apex ventrally is noted.  There is extensive heterotopic ossification
about the distal femur, which could be suggestive of prior callus formation
and injury, though an acute fracture component cannot be completely excluded. 
No discrete focal lytic or sclerotic osseous abnormality is otherwise
detected.  There appears to be a small joint effusion.  The osseous structures
are diffusely demineralized.  Prominent superior patellar enthesophyte is
noted.  No radiopaque foreign body.  No osseous destruction is identified to
suggest osteomyelitis.

IMPRESSION:


1. Impacted distal femoral metadiaphysis fracture with dorsal displacement and
ventral angulation of the fracture apex.  Extensive heterotopic ossification
about the distal femur suggests prior callus formation and prior injury,
however given the distinct fracture margins, an acute fracture component is
not excluded.
2. No definite radiographic evidence for osteomyelitis.

Moderate quantity of stool seen in the ascending and transverse colon.

Supine assessment limits detection for free air; there is no gross
pneumoperitoneum.

No evidence of acute osseous abnormality. Lumbar scoliosis is present.

There is an implanted device located in the left middle abdomen with wires
projecting over the lumbar spine and may represent a spinal nerve stimulator

physical exam is recommended.  Otherwise there are no unexplained soft tissue
calcifications or radiopaque foreign bodies.
